title: Growth and displacement of planar self-avoiding walks: a conditional identification
statement: For the uniform probability on nearest-neighbor self-avoiding walks \(\gamma\) of fixed length \(n\) from the origin in \(\mathbb Z^2\), determine the asymptotic order of \(\mathbb E\|\gamma_n\|\) and the square-lattice connective constant \(\mu=\lim c_n^{1/n}\). This is a definite modern problem associated with the ambiguous notebook rule, which might instead mean nonbacktracking or kinetic growth.
status: As of November 2026: the uniform-SAW interpretation is sub-ballistic by \citet[Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2]{duminil2013subballistic}, first posted May 2012 and published October 2013. The conjectural square-lattice endpoint exponent \(3/4\) is not a theorem in the reviewed sources. The proposed count base \(e\) is already excluded by the rigorous 2000 bound \(\mu\le2.679192495\) of \citet{ponitz2000bounds}; an exact square-lattice constant is not obtained. Nonbacktracking walks have the different count \(4\cdot3^{n-1}\). The later published bound is \(\mu\le2.662343\), from \citet{couronne2025bound} (preprint first posted 29 November 2022; journal publication 31 October 2025). An author-posted preprint of 21 October 2026, \citet{tomar2026connective}, claims \(\mu\le2.6586513\); its certificate was not independently rerun here. Neither value is an exact determination of the square-lattice constant.

title: Invariant solutions for invariant data
statement: Given a group acting on distributions and an equivariant differential operator \(P\), does the solvability of \(Pu=f\) for invariant \(f\) imply solvability by an invariant \(u\)?
status: As of November 2026: true for compact groups by averaging; false without further hypotheses for noncompact groups. Translations of \(\mathbb R\), \(P=d/dx\), \(f=1\) give an elementary counterexample. The Lorentz action discussed in \citet{methee1954lorentz} is a structured special case, whose full surjectivity theorem was not read in this run.

title: Fundamental solutions of invariant operators on groups
statement: For a specified left-invariant differential operator \(P\) on a Lie group \(G\), determine whether a distribution \(E\) exists with \(PE=\delta_e\). On a compact group, distinguish this equation from its reduced version with the constant or null-space projection removed.
status: As of November 2026: a universal positive answer is false. Complex invariant Lewy-type operators can be locally nonsolvable on noncompact groups; compact groups have zero-mode and representation-theoretic obstructions. \citet[Theorem 1]{cerezo1969fundamental} gives a compact-group criterion. For \(\partial_x-\alpha\partial_y\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), the reduced distributional problem is governed by the polynomial small-divisor condition in \citet{greenfield1972global}; the unreduced delta equation fails for every slope.

title: Extreme tracial characters of SL2 over the rationals
statement: Classify extreme normalized positive-definite class functions on the discrete group \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Q)\). The source initially says only two-by-two rational matrices; the later determinant-one formula motivates, but does not prove, this precise interpretation.
status: As of November 2026: solved by \citet[Theorem 2.4]{petersonthom2016characters}, preprint March 2013, online publication March 2014, print July 2016. The extreme characters are the trivial character and the two central characters extended by zero off \(\{\pm I\}\). The result does not claim a classification of the entire unitary dual or an unqualified \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Q)\) problem.

title: Index of nonlinear Fredholm maps
statement: A \(C^1\) map \(F:M\to N\) of Banach manifolds is Fredholm if every \(DF_x\) is Fredholm. Its derivative index is locally constant, hence constant on connected \(M\). This does not define vector-space kernels or cokernels for \(F\) itself.
status: As of November 2026, Fredholm-map theory supplies the precise answer in this framework.

title: Stable index of a continuous Fredholm family
statement: For norm-continuous \(T:X\to\operatorname{Fred}(H)\), with compact Hausdorff \(X\), choose finite-dimensional \(V\) with \(T_xH+V=H\). Then \(E_x=T_x^{-1}V\) is a bundle and \([E]-[X\times V]\in K^0(X)\) is independent of \(V\).
status: As of November 2026, the index bundle answers the stable question; its rank is the numerical index.

title: Invariant subspaces of bounded Hilbert-space operators
statement: Does every bounded linear operator on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space \(H\) admit a closed invariant subspace \(M\) with \(0\ne M\ne H\)?
status: As of 12 November 2026, no generally accepted solution was verified in the literature checked. \citet[Introduction]{marcoux2026generators}, first posted 21 August 2026, explicitly states this Hilbert-space question as unsolved. The 1964 announcement \citep{debrangesrovnyak1964existence} was retracted in 1965 \citep{debrangesrovnyak1965correction}; these records are bibliographically verified, not treated as valid proofs. Polynomially compact and other special classes in record 50 do not settle the unrestricted question.

title: Coordinate generators for the ball-algebra maximal ideal
statement: For \(A(B^n)=\mathcal O(B^n)\cap C(\overline B^n)\) and \(a\in B^n\), the ideal \(\{f:f(a)=0\}\) is generated by \(z_j-a_j\). The source asks \(n=2,a=0\).
status: As of November 2026, the exact ball question is solved; later counterexamples concern other domains.

title: Does Koopman spectrum determine a finite ergodic group action?
statement: The answer is negative even for transitive finite actions. Let \(G=GL(3,\mathbb F_2)\) act on the seven nonzero vectors of \(\mathbb F_2^3\), and on the seven nonzero covectors by the dual action. The permutation characters coincide, but the \(G\)-sets are not isomorphic. With uniform probability these are ergodic systems with unitarily equivalent Koopman representations.
status: As of November 2026, the finite-group question has a negative answer; this is not an open reconstruction problem.

title: Primitivity of universal enveloping algebras
statement: For a Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), when does \(U(\mathfrak g)\) have a faithful irreducible module? For the finite-dimensional complex reconstruction, this asks whether its zero prime ideal is primitive.
status: As of November 2026: established primitive-ideal theory gives the Dixmier--Moeglin criterion in the finite-dimensional complex case. The source omits field and dimension, so the audit does not assert an unrestricted field-independent answer.

title: Isomorphism of Weyl algebras of different ranks
statement: For characteristic-zero \(k\), can \(A_m(k)\cong A_n(k)\) as \(k\)-algebras with \(m\ne n\)? The notebook asks \(m=1,n=2\).
status: Solved: no. Growth dimension \(2n\) distinguishes the rank; Gelfand--Kirillov, received January 1966, published 1966. Status checked November 2026.

title: Trace of a commutator
statement: Under what hypotheses on bounded \(A,B\) and the trace is \(\operatorname{Tr}[A,B]=0\)?
status: As of November 2026: both products trace class suffice; trace class of the commutator alone does not, as \([S^*,S]\) shows. Later trace formulas treat the nonvanishing case.

title: Invariant subspaces for subnormal operators
statement: Does every bounded subnormal operator on a complex Hilbert space of dimension greater than one admit a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace?
status: As of November 2026: solved affirmatively by \citet{brown1978subnormal}, published in September 1978. The publisher's abstract explicitly states the affirmative theorem; the full subscription article was not read in this audit. The notebook's then-open special-class question is distinct from the unrestricted Hilbert-space problem.

title: Weight criteria for a unicellular backward shift
statement: Characterize bounded nonzero weight sequences for which the backward shift on \(\ell^2\) has exactly the finite initial-span invariant subspaces and the whole space.
status: As of November 2026: developed and partly answered in verified weight classes, including monotone moduli tending to zero. The scope of a universal explicit arbitrary-weight criterion was not ascertained in this audit; it is not declared solved or open by default.

title: An invariant-subspace lattice with a bilateral integer chain
statement: Does a bounded Hilbert-space operator have full invariant-subspace lattice \(\{0,H\}\cup\{M_m:m\in\mathbb Z\}\), with strict successive inclusion, intersection zero and dense union?
status: As of November 2026: yes. Domar\textquotesingle s Theorem~2 (1981) gives an exact example; \(Se_j=\exp(-2|2j+1|)e_{j+1}\) on \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z)\) has precisely the coordinate-tail nest and the two endpoints.

title: Invariant subspaces of every irrational Bishop operator
statement: For every irrational \(\alpha\), must \(T_\alpha f(x)=x f(\{x+\alpha\})\) on \(L^2(0,1)\) have a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace?
status: Affirmative for non-Liouville parameters and a larger arithmetic class, including the continued-fraction condition in Chamizo et al., Theorem 3.7. No established all-parameter resolution was verified through November 2026.

title: Cyclicity of irrational Bishop operators
statement: Does every irrational Bishop operator admit a cyclic vector, and for which parameters is the constant function cyclic?
status: Béhani proves a co-meager cyclic parameter set and sufficient approximation conditions. The chapter develops a bounded rational-orbit certificate and continuity estimates. It does not prove universal irrational cyclicity; an inaccessible 2026 lead is not relied on.
